from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = [
            "Sequential processing limits memory for long sentences.",
            "RNNs forget early information as they progress.",
            "A conveyor belt model loses context over time.",
            "Attention provides a new way to process input.",
            "Parallel processing enables global context for every word."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Problem: Why Old Models Forget", lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a central text element
        problem_text = Text("Old Models Forget", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(problem_text, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(problem_text))
        self.play(problem_text.animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fade in a series of sequential data blocks
        blocks = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(4)])
        blocks.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(blocks, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(blocks))
        self.play(blocks.animate.set_color("#4169E1"))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#4169E1"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show a 'bottleneck' effect
        bottleneck = Polygon(np.array([-0.5, 0.5, 0]), np.array([0.5, 0.5, 0]), np.array([0.2, -0.5, 0]), np.array([-0.2, -0.5, 0]), color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(bottleneck, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(bottleneck))
        self.play(bottleneck.animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Query searches for information we need.",
            "The Key is the label on each book.",
            "The Value contains the actual requested content."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize mobjects
        q = Square(side_length=1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).add(Text("Q", font_size=24))
        k = Square(side_length=1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).add(Text("K", font_size=24))
        v = Square(side_length=1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).add(Text("V", font_size=24))
        
        q_label = Text("Query", font_size=20)
        k_label = Text("Key", font_size=20)
        v_label = Text("Value", font_size=20)
        
        # Group and place
        q_group = VGroup(q, q_label).arrange(DOWN)
        k_group = VGroup(k, k_label).arrange(DOWN)
        v_group = VGroup(v, v_label).arrange(DOWN)
        
        self.place_at_grid(q_group, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(k_group, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(v_group, 'B6')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(q_group), FadeIn(k_group), FadeIn(v_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#32CD32")) # LimeGreen
        self.play(q.animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF")) # White
        self.play(q_group.animate.next_to(k_group, LEFT, buff=0.5))
        self.play(k.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700")) # Gold
        self.play(v.animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(v_group.animate.scale(1.2))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Math: Dot-Product Attention", [
            "Scores measure similarity between Queries and Keys.",
            "Higher dot-products indicate stronger relevance scores.",
            "Softmax converts scores into percentage weightings."
        ])
        
        # Formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V
        formula = MathTex(
            r"\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V",
            font_size=36
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Define parts for color changes
        formula.set_color(WHITE)
        qk_t = formula.get_part_by_tex("QK^T")
        sqrt_dk = formula.get_part_by_tex(r"\sqrt{d_k}")
        softmax = formula.get_part_by_tex(r"\text{softmax}")
        v = formula[-1]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            qk_t.animate.set_color("#00CED1"),
            sqrt_dk.animate.set_color("#FFD700")
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            softmax.animate.set_color("#FF4500"),
            v.animate.set_color("#32CD32")
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Weighing inputs enables deep contextual understanding.",
            "This captures meaning even for complex sentences.",
            "Transformers achieve state-of-the-art results through attention."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: Contextual Understanding", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        sentence = VGroup(
            Text("The"), Text("robot"), Text("picked"), Text("up"), Text("the"), Text("wrench"), Text("because"), Text("it"), Text("was"), Text("heavy.")
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(sentence, 'B1', 'B6')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(sentence))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        link1 = Line(sentence[1].get_bottom(), sentence[7].get_bottom(), color="#00CED1")
        link2 = Line(sentence[5].get_bottom(), sentence[7].get_bottom(), color="#00CED1")
        self.play(Create(link1), Create(link2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        box = SurroundingRectangle(sentence, color="#FFD700", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read

sections.title: The Problem: Why Old Models Forget
sections.content: Introduce the limitation of sequential processing (RNNs). Explain that as sentences grow, early information fades. Use a prerequisite visual: a 'conveyor belt' vs. a 'cocktail party'.
sections.example: A reader tries to memorize a 100-page book by reading one word at a time, forgetting the start by the time they reach the end.

sections.title: The Intuition: The Cocktail Party Effect
sections.content: Explain that Attention allows the model to look at all words simultaneously and decide which are relevant to the current word. Visual: Connecting lines of varying thickness between words in a sentence.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' when the model processes 'it', it draws a thick 'attention' line to 'animal' and a thin one to 'street'.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
sections.content: Break down the core math into an analogy: A library system. Query (what I want), Key (what the book label says), Value (the content of the book). Visual: A search bar searching for a specific book tag.
sections.example: You (Query) look at book labels (Keys) to find the content (Value) that matches your request.

sections.title: The Math: Dot-Product Attention
sections.content: Simplify the mathematical operation: Score = Q × Kᵀ. Explain the Softmax function as a way to convert scores into percentages (weights). Visual: A heatmap showing intensity values that sum to 100%.
sections.example: If the Query 'it' matches 'animal' with high intensity, the model assigns 0.9 weight to 'animal' and 0.1 to 'street'.

sections.title: Application: Contextual Understanding
sections.content: Summarize how this enables LLMs to generate coherent text. By weighing inputs, the model understands polysemy (words with multiple meanings) and long-range dependencies.
sections.example: An AI assistant reading a manual: 'The robot picked up the wrench because it was heavy.' Attention ensures the AI knows the *wrench* is heavy, not the *robot*.
